body:
Source: GitHub issue #970 (bug), triage comment https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/issues/970#issuecomment-5527069417. D1 (exports map / dispatch.mjs package.json resolution) and D4 (deny fires on read-only commands) are ALREADY FIXED on main by PR #965 (squash-merged as 982adee7) — do NOT touch packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs's shellPathCandidates/evaluateHandoffPreToolUse read-only classifier, do NOT re-add an exports-map fallback, do NOT re-derive those fixes. This ticket is the REMAINING scope only: D2/D3 (general-case packaging-fault reporting), the systematic package.json-resolution regression test, D5 (unusable remediation instructions), D6 (denial text embeds a directly-runnable mutating bypass command), D7 (adlc init mislabels the harness), D8 (undocumented insecure init default), D9 (version-floor doc misplacement).

Re-verified on main @ 982adee7:

D2/D3 — packages/cli/lib/dispatch.mjs:182-191 `runBin(label, bin, args, spawnFn)`: when `bin` is falsy (packageJsonPath()/resolvePackageBin() returned null for ANY reason — genuine absence, or the entry-based fallback also failing) it always returns the generic `tool not installed: ${label} - run "npm i -g @adlc/cli" to install the suite`, with no `err.code`, no distinction between "never installed" and "installed but a packaging fault prevented resolution". `packageJsonPath()` (same file, ~line 56-79) already discards the specific error into a bare `null` return on both rungs.

Systematic regression AC — packages/cli/test/dispatch.test.mjs currently has two hand-picked regression tests (`@adlc/context-handoff` + a `@adlc/rails-guard` control) added by #965, not a sweep of every `@adlc/*` package. A packed-tarball CI harness is OUT OF SCOPE for this ticket (too large a lift); the delivered AC is an in-repo systematic test instead — see AC3 below.

D5/D6 — the mutating recovery command is built by `formatRecoveryCommand` in packages/context-handoff/lib/recovery-exception.mjs:327-337 (`return \`${interpreterDisplay} ${scriptDisplay} bypass --session ${sessionId} --write\`;`), consumed directly by pi/opencode via `@adlc/context-handoff`'s exports, and MIRRORED (a "KEEP IN SYNC" twin, per that file's own comments) into plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/handoff-gate.mjs and the codex/pi equivalents — each has its own `*-helper-drift.test.mjs` under packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/ that fails if a twin falls out of sync with the canonical file, so edit the canonical file first and let the drift tests name every twin that needs the identical change. The assembled deny message (plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs:2333-2336, and the equivalent construction in the codex/pi/opencode hooks) reads: `mutation denied (...). Resume via host \`adlc handoff resume\` / repair, or continue in a fresh session. ... ${recoveryDiagnostic(sessionId)}` — same-session `adlc handoff resume` exits 2 by design (recovery-exception.mjs's own resume subcommand contract), so the FIRST-listed remediation in the message is the one guaranteed not to work in the state it's read. `bypass --write` additionally requires `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` (packages/context-handoff/bin/handoff.mjs) to mutate at all — in a repo where that key IS exported to the agent's shell (this repo, dogfooding), the printed command is a real, complete, directly-runnable weakening of the gate handed to the agent at the moment of maximum incentive (ADLC.md rule 6: agents must never weaken a gate). The printed command's self-contained, package-resolution-independent construction is DELIBERATE hardening (see the "Round-5 review" comment above `recoveryDiagnostic` in adlc-hook.mjs, fixing issue #526's "stranded with only pwd" regression) — do not remove or break that self-containment; the fix is in WHAT gets printed automatically vs. what requires a deliberate extra step, not in HOW the command resolves its own paths.

D7 — packages/init/lib/scaffold.mjs:15-24 `configForHarness(harness)`: a three-way ternary that special-cases only `cursor` and `copilot`; every other value — including `null` (no `--harness` flag given), `'codex'`, and any value that isn't cursor/copilot — silently becomes `{ codex: { railEnforcement: 'auto' } }`. packages/init/bin/adlc-init.mjs:5,25-27 only accepts `--harness codex|cursor|copilot` at the CLI level — there is no way to register `claude-code`, `pi`, `opencode`, or `gemini` at all. The issue's repro ran `adlc init` (no flag) inside a Claude Code session and got a config claiming `codex`.

D8 — packages/init/lib/scaffold.mjs:24: `securityMode: 'unsigned-fallback'` is hardcoded into every freshly scaffolded config with only an internal code comment ("securityMode is required for config-integrity once a config is committed") explaining why it exists, nothing about what it WEAKENS, and no docs.

D9 — docs/integrations/codex.md:9-13 states the `@adlc/cli` 1.11.0-or-newer / context-rot-handoff-exports version floor only in Codex's own Install section, though `@adlc/cli` is shared by all seven harness integrations (claude-code.md, cursor.md, opencode.md, pi.md, gemini.md, copilot.md carry no equivalent note). NOTE: since PR #966 (merged/pending — disconnects the context-rot handoff hook's automatic wiring for claude-code/codex/pi/opencode behind an env-var kill switch, default off), the ORIGINAL reason this floor was framed as "the handoff gate hard-requires it" no longer describes the shipped default — reframe the shared note around general `@adlc/cli`/`@adlc/*` version-matching (`ADLC releases the CLI and every harness plugin in lockstep; install matching major.minor versions`) rather than repeating the now-inactive-by-default handoff-gate framing verbatim.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Packages/dirs touched: `packages/cli` (bin `adlc`, lib `dispatch.mjs` — dispatcher only, no other lib files need touching), `packages/context-handoff` (lib `recovery-exception.mjs` is the canonical remediation-text/command builder; `adapter-test/*-helper-drift.test.mjs` are the sync guards — do not hand-edit the twins, let the drift tests fail and then apply the identical diff), `packages/init` (lib `scaffold.mjs`, bin `adlc-init.mjs`), `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks` (twin `handoff-gate.mjs`, message assembly in `adlc-hook.mjs`), `plugins/adlc-codex/hooks`, `plugins/adlc-pi/lib` (their own twins/consumers, found by running the drift tests), `docs/integrations/*.md`. Tests: `node --test packages/cli/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test packages/init/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/*.test.mjs`, `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/*.test.mjs` — run every one, not just the package you think you touched, since the drift tests live under context-handoff but pin claude-code/codex/pi files.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. D2/D3: `packageJsonPath()` and `packageJsonFromEntry()` in dispatch.mjs stop discarding the specific failure. Introduce a typed result (e.g. `{ path, code }` where `code` is one of `'not-a-dependency'` (require.resolve threw MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the bare specifier — genuinely not installed) or `'packaging-fault'` (resolved as a dependency but no package.json could be located by any rung — an exports/layout defect) — or equivalent; keep `packageJsonPath`'s existing plain-string-or-null return for its other callers if that's less churn, and thread the classified code through a NEW function `resolvePackageBinDiagnostic` (or similar) that `runBin`'s caller uses only for the error MESSAGE, not the resolution logic itself. `runBin`'s message becomes: for `'packaging-fault'`, name the real defect ("<label> is installed but its package.json could not be resolved (packaging fault) — this is not fixed by reinstalling") instead of suggesting `npm i -g @adlc/cli`; for `'not-a-dependency'`/genuine absence, keep today's message. Exit code stays 1 (operational error) for both — this is a message-quality fix, not a new exit path.
2. D5/D6: In `packages/context-handoff/lib/recovery-exception.mjs`, split `formatRecoveryCommand`'s output into two: a primary line recommending recovery in a FRESH session or subagent FIRST (this always works, needs no key, no same-session restriction), and the mutating command printed only in its DRY-RUN form (`bypass --session <id>` — no `--write`), with a separate, clearly-labeled sentence stating that `--write` requires a human operator holding `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` to add `--write` themselves after reviewing why the deny fired — the assembled string must not contain the literal substring `--write` as part of a single directly-copy-pasteable line. `formatNoSessionIdMessage`/`formatUnsafeInstallPathMessage` degrade analogously (no full mutating command). Apply the identical text/logic change to every twin the relevant `*-helper-drift.test.mjs` flags (claude-code, codex, pi) — run the drift tests to enumerate them, do not guess. Do not touch `bypass`'s actual CLI implementation in `bin/handoff.mjs` (the `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` gate on `--write` itself is out of scope — this ticket is about what the DENY MESSAGE prints automatically, not the CLI's own auth). Also fix the ordering in the assembled deny message (adlc-hook.mjs:2333 and its per-host equivalents): lead with "continue in a fresh session / subagent" before naming `adlc handoff resume`, and where the message names `adlc handoff resume`, note explicitly that it must be run from a DIFFERENT session than the one that hit the deny (same-session exits 2).
3. D7: Extend `--harness` in packages/init/bin/adlc-init.mjs to accept `claude-code`, `pi`, `opencode`, `gemini` in addition to the existing `codex`, `cursor`, `copilot` (update the usage string too). In `configForHarness`, use the passed harness value directly for every accepted name (stop defaulting non-cursor/non-copilot values to `codex`); `codex` stays the literal default ONLY when `harness` is `null`/unset AND unset must now also print a `warnings[]` entry (surfaced by `adlc init`'s existing `result.warnings` reporting path, `bin/adlc-init.mjs:45-52` — do not add a new output channel) telling the operator to pass `--harness <name>` explicitly, naming which harnesses are recognized, rather than silently mislabeling. This does not add auto-detection (out of scope, a bigger feature) — it removes the SILENT mislabel and gives every harness a real way to be registered correctly.
4. D8: Add a one-paragraph doc comment above the `securityMode: 'unsigned-fallback'` literal in `configForHarness` (already partially present — extend it) plus user-facing documentation (README.md's init section or docs/tools/init.md, whichever exists — check both) stating literally what `unsigned-fallback` weakens (unsigned manifest entries are accepted; see docs/specs/manifest-key-hermeticity.md or the nearest canonical spec for the precise contract) and that a repo intending to sign gate evidence must set a stronger mode explicitly. Do not change the default value itself (that's a breaking-change decision out of scope for a bug-fix ticket) — confirm-and-document only.
5. D9: Replace docs/integrations/codex.md:9-13's version-floor paragraph with a short pointer to a new shared "## Version requirements" section added near the top of docs/toolkit.md (after the Lifecycle map), reframed around general `@adlc/cli`/`@adlc/*` lockstep versioning per the note above (NOT restating the now-default-off handoff-gate framing as the forcing reason). Add one linking sentence to the Install (or equivalent) section of docs/integrations/claude-code.md, cursor.md, opencode.md, pi.md, gemini.md, copilot.md pointing at the same shared section — mechanical, one line each, do not restate the paragraph seven times.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `runBin()` names the real defect for a packaging fault vs genuine absence; the generic npm-reinstall suggestion only appears for genuine absence. verify: `node --test packages/cli/test/dispatch.test.mjs`
- AC2 A regression test proves the OLD message class (silently identical wording for both failure classes) would fail against the new code — i.e. the test distinguishes the two paths, not just asserts new wording exists. verify: `node --test packages/cli/test/dispatch.test.mjs`
- AC3 Systematic in-repo regression: every `@adlc/*` package under `packages/*` whose `package.json` declares an `exports` map is resolved successfully via the dispatch.mjs resolution path (iterate `packages/*/package.json`, skip packages with no `exports` field, assert `packageJsonPath`/`packageJsonFromEntry` finds each — this generalizes #965's two hand-picked cases into a sweep, without requiring a packed tarball). verify: `node --test packages/cli/test/dispatch.test.mjs`
- AC4 A deny message's remediation text never contains a directly copy-pasteable line with `--write` in it; a fresh-session/subagent recommendation appears before the same-session-restricted `adlc handoff resume` mention. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs` (new test in an existing or new file) plus `node --test packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*-helper-drift.test.mjs`
- AC5 `adlc init --harness claude-code|pi|opencode|gemini` records that exact harness in the generated config (not `codex`); `adlc init` with no `--harness` flag emits a warning naming the recognized harness values, and still writes a usable config (`codex` remains the literal default value, now WARNED rather than silent). verify: `node --test packages/init/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC6 `securityMode: 'unsigned-fallback'` is documented (what it weakens) both in-code and in user-facing docs; default value unchanged. verify: `grep -c "unsigned-fallback" packages/init/README.md docs/tools/init.md` (or wherever init's docs live — locate first) each >= 1, plus existing init tests still green
- AC7 The 1.11.0 version-floor statement exists in exactly one shared location (`docs/toolkit.md`) and every one of the 7 harness integration docs links to it (codex.md's own copy is replaced, not duplicated). verify: `grep -c "Version requirement" docs/toolkit.md docs/integrations/claude-code.md docs/integrations/codex.md docs/integrations/cursor.md docs/integrations/opencode.md docs/integrations/pi.md docs/integrations/gemini.md docs/integrations/copilot.md` each >= 1
- AC8 Existing suites green across every touched package/plugin (see CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER's test list — run ALL of them, the drift tests are the ones most likely to be missed). verify: `node --test packages/cli/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*.test.mjs packages/init/test/*.test.mjs plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/*.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/*.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC9 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: D1 (exports map / dispatch.mjs resolution fallback) and D4 (read-only-command false-positive classifier) — already fixed by #965/982adee7, do not touch `evaluateHandoffPreToolUse`'s read-only ladder or re-add an exports-map entry. Auto-detecting the calling harness in `adlc init` (only explicit `--harness` + an honest warning on absence, per NORMATIVE #3). Changing `unsigned-fallback` as the actual default value (document only). A packed-tarball CI harness for AC3 (in-repo sweep only). Changing `bin/handoff.mjs`'s own `ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY` gate on `--write` (message-only fix). Any other sibling issue in these packages not named above.
title: deny-remediation: packaging-fault reporting, unusable/unsafe recovery text, init harness mislabel, docs
